name: Satire
overview: The Scriptures present satire as a means to expose human folly and provoke reflection, exemplified in the painful interactions between Hannah and Peninnah. Hannah’s adversary provoked her deeply because the LORD had closed her womb, causing sorrow and bitterness (1 Samuel 1:6-10). Yet even in this trial, the narrative reveals God's sovereignty and love, as Hannah’s husband tries to comfort her, highlighting the tension between human weakness and divine purpose (1 Samuel 1:8). This context shows how satire can reveal the hardness of heart in others while pointing believers to trust in God's providence and grace.
